items.prompt: Why does DOWN use floor quotient here?

options.why: Binary exactness is not assumed; the computation parses decimal cents and uses integer division.
The supplied domain is nonnegative, not negative rates; negative inputs would require separate rounding reasoning.
Ties can occur, but DOWN truncates every nonnegative fractional part without applying a tie rule.
For nonnegative fee cents, truncation toward zero equals floor, so the quotient implements DOWN in this domain.

items.explanation: Toward zero and floor coincide for the nonnegative inputs in this task; they differ for some negative values.
